subject: INLA implementation for I00K non-Gaussian point-referenced data

messages.author: 85f5146e584efdd5
messages.subject: INLA implementation for I00K non-Gaussian point-referenced data
parts:
Dear all, 

I am trying to implement INLA for massive non-Gaussian point-referenced data (n=100K). When I made a mesh, I used cutoff=0.05 and it takes about 10 hours from my personal desktop. 

To make this faster, I made a fewer number of the mesh by changing cutoff=0.1 (Please see the following code). However, this choice of cutoff makes an error message. The followings are part of my code.

#############################################################
## Define Mesh using Coordinates
 observations lower-center area of map
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(gridLocation, max.edge=c(1,1),cutoff=0.1)  # no error at 0.05
AMat <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc=gridLocation)  
AMatCV <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc=predLocation)  
dim(AMat)

# Model fitting
spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh=mesh, alpha=2)
stk.e <- inla.stack(tag='est', ## tag
                    data=list(y=Z), ## response
                    A=list(AMat, 1), ## two projector matrix
                    effects=list(## two elements:
                      s=1:spde$n.spde, ## RF index
                      data.frame( x1=XMat[,1],x2=XMat[,2])))
# Prediction fitting
stk.pred <- inla.stack(tag='pred', A=list(AMatCV, 1), 
                       data=list(y=NA), ## response as NA
                       effects=list(s=1:spde$n.spde, 
                                    data.frame(x1=Xpreds[,1],x2=Xpreds[,2])))

stk.full <- inla.stack(stk.e, stk.pred)
formula <- y ~ 0  + x1 + x2 +## fixed part
             f(s, model=spde) ## RF term
link = c(rep(NA, n),rep(1, n.pred))
res<-inla(formula,
          data=inla.stack.data(stk.full, spde=spde),
          family="binomial",  #binomial, poisson
          control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.full), compute=TRUE, link=link),
          keep=FALSE, verbose=TRUE)
#############################################################

When I do that, I get the error message,

outpuError in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : The inla-program exited with an error. 

There was no error when I used cutoff 0.05. But when I change the cutoff to 0.1 to make my code faster, I receive an error message. In fact I tried cutoff 0.09, 0.08, 0.07, 0.06 then they gave the same error message. 

Do you know why it happens? 

Thanks, 

Jaewoo
